title: Ardent Financial - POC scoping: workload modeling
summary: POC scoping call to align on workload characterization for an Ardent Financial POC. Discussed expected QPS, concurrency, typical prompt/request sizes (input tokens) and response sizes (output tokens), target latency SLOs, acceptable cost envelopes, and benchmark plan. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot with synthetic and replayed traffic, Redwood to share benchmark spreadsheet and security docs, Ardent to provide sample traffic and success metrics.
next_steps: Redwood to share benchmark spreadsheet and example workload templates by 2027-04-01
Ardent to send 3 days of anonymized request logs (sample) by 2027-04-03
Schedule pilot kickoff and perf benchmark window (2 weeks) w/c 2027-04-11
Redwood to provide cost estimate for hosted vs dedicated profiles by 2027-04-05
Exchange security questionnaire and SOC2 evidence links
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-03-29 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m | Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Ardent Head of ML), Ethan Cole (Platform Eng), Sofia (CTO)

[00:00] Lena: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros \u0002 i'm lena, account exec at Redwood.
[00:06] Marcus: morning, marcus here, solutions eng. i'll drive the workload side and benchmarks.
[00:10] Priya: hi all, priya \u0002 i'll be the day-to-day owner for the POC, focused on model quality and perf.
[00:15] Ethan: ethan, infra/platf, i'll handle networking and capacity questions.
[00:18] Sofia: sofia here, scope and success criteria sign-off.
[00:22] Lena: great. goal today is to nail down QPS, concurrency, token sizes, success metrics and timeline so we can size the pilot and propose profiles.
[00:30] Marcus: quick clarifying question: are we planning to run on hosted first or straight to dedicated / vpc?
[00:36] Priya: we'd prefer hosted to start to move faster, but if latency or data residency is an issue we may need private. So we want numbers to decide.
[00:44] Ethan: yes, also we have strict KMS rules and need audit log detail \u0002 but for benching we can use hosted test account.
[00:50] Marcus: perfect. can you give rough traffic shape? qps, burstiness, typical concurrency?
[00:56] Priya: two parts \u0002 synchronous chat style UI and async batch summarization. For chat: steady 40 qps average during peak window, peaks to 120 qps for 10 mins, per-request concurrency around 60 concurrent sessions. For batch: 5 jobs per hour, each job submits ~2k documents, but those are off-peak.
[01:18] Marcus: good. and token sizes for chat?
[01:22] Priya: prompt templates average 120 tokens in, responses average 220 tokens out. But we have a long-tail \u0002 about 5% go over 1k output tokens (rare).
[01:33] Marcus: ok, that's helpful. what about context window? full convo history is sent for some users \u0002 typical context length ~2k tokens.
[01:40] Priya: yes some power users keep long threads. we can sample and truncate, but need KV cache behavior accounted for.
[01:46] Ethan: network constraints: VPC peering is doable for private later; for hosted perf testing we need egress allowlist for the test infra.
[01:54] Marcus: noted. on latency SLOs what are you targeting?
[01:58] Sofia: for chat we want p95 under 300ms token generation if possible, or overall reply under 800ms. For summarization batch it's ok to be longer.
[02:10] Marcus: p95 300ms token gen is aggressive given 220 tokens out typical \u0002 depends on model size and batching. We can try smaller model variants and quantization to meet cost/latency.
[02:20] Lena: and what's the acceptable cost envelope?
[02:23] Sofia: we'd like initial POC to show < $0.01 per chat response on average (including in/out tokens), but we can be flexible if quality needs a bigger model.
[02:33] Marcus: good to know. for benchmarking we'll run variants: open LLM small (quantized), mid-size, and our recommended production profile. We'll measure throughput (qps), latency percentiles, and tokens/sec.
[02:44] Priya: can you run prefix caching tests? a lot of our users reuse templates and earlier convo KV hits should reduce costs.
[02:50] Marcus: yes we can include KV/prefix cache scenarios. we'll do cold start vs warm cache.
[02:55] Ethan: when you say qps, are you counting question-level requests or token-level? we need to align.
[03:00] Marcus: qps is requests per second; tokens/sec we'll report separately. we'll also report per-request token counts distribution.
[03:06] Priya: ideal outcomes for the POC: 1) we can hit p95 latency targets for 80% of peak traffic using hosted with recommended profile, 2) cost comes in under your threshold or the dedicated alternative gives clear ROI, 3) any security gaps are documented.
[03:21] Marcus: noted. recommended success criteria: define concrete numbers \u0002 e.g., p95 reply <800ms for 80% of peak requests, 99th under 1.5s, cost per 1k tokens < $X, and end-to-end integration with our telemetry.
[03:36] Sofia: that sounds reasonable. can you propose exact cost per profile?
[03:40] Lena: we'll produce a small cost matrix \u0002 hosted baseline, hosted with caching & batching, and a dedicated reserved profile.
[03:48] Marcus: on workload modeling we'll need: a) sample request logs (anonymized) for token hist, b) QPS by minute for a typical week, c) identification of heavy users and the % of long responses.
[03:59] Priya: we can extract a 3-day sample and strip PII; we'll aim to send that by next friday.
[04:06] Ethan: timer \u0002 what benchmarking infra do you need from our side?
[04:09] Marcus: ideally a test API key and allowlisted IPs for the runner; we'll drive synthetic replay and also run a replay test using your logs. memory of the KV cache will be simulated by replaying session ids.
[04:20] Priya: ok. also we have enterprise compliance check \u0002 can you share SOC2 links and the redwood security pack?
[04:25] Lena: yes, we'll share the security pack and our SOC2 summary. for private deployment we can discuss VPC + KMS later.
[04:32] Marcus: timeline proposal: share benchmark spreadsheet & test plan within 3 business days, receive sample logs within 5, pilot kickoff week of 2027-04-11, run 2-week benchmark window, final results and recommendation by end of April.
[04:46] Sofia: constraints: procurement needs cost estimates for hosted vs dedicated before contract. also we need a simple SLA ask for the POC.
[04:53] Lena: we'll include an informal uptime target for the pilot and a cost estimate.
[04:58] Marcus: technical notes for the bench: we'll test three model families, tokenize distributions, cold vs warm cache, batching factors, and autoscale thresholds. We'll capture per-route token counts, tokens/sec, GPU utilization and throttling.
[05:13] Ethan: do you need synthetic prompt generators or we'll provide real templates?
[05:17] Marcus: both \u0002 synthetic to hit peaks and replay to validate real-world distribution. the synthetic generator will model the 95/75/50/median token sizes you give us.
[05:26] Priya: we have some long tail heavy requests \u0002 about 5% above 1k output tokens as i said \u0002 please ensure the bench covers that.
[05:32] Marcus: will do. also we recommend sampling for model variants: 1) quantized 8-bit mid-size, 2) float16 larger model, 3) a 70B family if quality demands.
[05:43] Priya: curious \u0002 how much improvement do you expect from prefix caching?
[05:47] Marcus: it depends; we've seen 20-40% token cost reduction on templated flows because fewer prompt tokens need to be regenerated, and latency improves since k-v cache avoids recomputing prior layers.
[05:58] Sofia: any red flags you see now?
[06:00] Marcus: main risks: long-tail responses blowing up cost, and concurrency spikes causing queuing if autoscale isn't tuned. We'll surface those in the spreadsheet and run stress tests.
[06:11] Lena: ok let's recap next steps \u0002 marcus, you'll share the benchmark plan and spreadsheet; lena will send security docs; ardent will send logs; schedule pilot kickoff week of 2027-04-11; redwood to send cost matrix.
[06:25] Marcus: actionables for bench: benchmark plan v1 by 2027-04-01, test account + allowlist details requested from ardent, will set up synthetic replay harness.
[06:36] Priya: we'll anonymize and send logs by 2027-04-03 and review the success criteria.
[06:42] Ethan: i'll coordinate networking and provide a list of IPs to allow.
[06:46] Lena: perfect. everyone ok with timeline?
[06:48] Sofia: yes.
[06:49] Lena: thanks all \u0002 we'll follow up with calendar invites and the spreadsheet.
[06:54] [end of recording]

Notes on transcription: some speaker boundaries auto-labeled; a few acronyms transcribed oddly (K M S, V P C). There was occasional cross-talk.

References & attached artifacts (links to be shared after call): - Redwood benchmark spreadsheet (to be shared) - Redwood security pack and SOC2 link - Example synthetic workload generator repo (link)

Recap (verbal): Redwood to run perf benchmarks (hosted profiles + dedicated baseline), measure QPS, concurrency, token distributions, cache warm/cold behavior, and provide recommendations and cost matrix. Ardent to supply anonymized logs and allowlisted IPs. Pilot kickoff target week of 2027-04-11, 2-week benchmark window, final recommendation end of April.
